classification_precision_spotcheck.method: 12 slides sampled (3 per deck) with random.seed(42) over the parsed slide list, judged by hand against family class + title + slide content.
classification_precision_spotcheck.result: 11/12 agreed with hand judgment after fixing 2 classifier bugs found during the spot-check (see caveats). 2/12 flagged as genuinely ambiguous boundary calls (concept-explanation vs practice-instruction) inherent to any class+title-only heuristic.
bugs_found_and_fixed: Substring match on family string caused 'is-recovery' (troubleshooting/annex slides) to false-match the '표지'(cover) keyword 'cover' (recovery contains cover as a substring). Fixed by switching to hyphen-segment exact-match instead of raw substring search.

'index-entry-slide' family was mapped to 구간전환(transition) via a generic 'index' keyword, but on inspection its title/content is a concept explanation of what index.html is, not a TOC/agenda slide. The 'index' keyword had exactly one match in the whole 4-deck corpus (this slide) and it was wrong, so the keyword was removed; the slide now falls through to the 개념설명 default, which is correct.
remaining_ambiguous_examples: W1_INITIAL #36 'Codex에서 폴더 열기' -- classified 개념설명, arguably 실습지시 (instructional title, no distinguishing class).
W1_MID #32 'file-verify-slide: 파일을 열어 직접 검증합니다' -- classified 개념설명, arguably 결과확인/실습지시 (imperative 'verify yourself' framing).

parser_known_limitations: Container detection is class-name-driven (card/box/panel/-row/-col/-case/-step/-side/-note/-item/-tile/-cell/-slot suffixes) plus a special-case for bare <article> tags added after discovering W1-final dense concept slides (e.g. S3CE, S39A) use un-classed <article> as their card-equivalent unit. Any OTHER un-classed repeating tag convention (e.g. bare <li> grids, bare <div> grids with only a parent grid class) is NOT recognized and will undercount container_count for that slide.

'family' = the slide's own class attribute with 'slide' removed, taken verbatim. This is the actual code-level layout identity, not the 8 canonical kit/layouts/families/*.md taxonomy names -- production decks use bespoke per-slide class names (e.g. 'llm-agent-wide', 'proc-stage canvas-fill') rather than the canonical family class names, so same-family-repetition figures measure literal CSS-class recurrence, not canonical-taxonomy recurrence.

'empty container' as literally defined by the task spec (0 chars, or <10 chars among >=2 same-class siblings) conflates two very different things: (a) legitimate image-only slots (class contains '-slot', holds a real with descriptive alt text -- NOT a defect) and (b) genuinely thin text cards. Reported separately as 'empty-image-slot' / 'empty-no-text-no-visual' / 'near-empty-sibling-*' -- see deck_quality_analysis.md. W1_MID's and most of W1_FINAL's 'empty container' count is dominated by (a), i.e. is NOT a quality problem; W2's entire empty-container count is type (b) (near-empty text-only cards), which IS the pattern the follow-up work should target.

'한 설명단위 평균 분할 장수' (avg multi-slide split length) could not be measured reliably. The chosen proxy (group consecutive 개념설명 slides by a 6-character title-prefix stem) found ZERO multi-slide runs in ALL FOUR decks -- Korean slide titles in this corpus are freely reworded per slide even when covering one continued topic, they do not share a lexical stem across a split. Reported as 1.0 for all four decks but this should be read as '확인불가' / method-null-result, not as evidence that no splitting occurs.

Text extraction excludes header/s-head, aria-hidden=true elements, and any element whose class matches nav|header|footer|pagenum|logo|progress|pd-dots|s-head|s-team|s-brand|s-line|s-logo. No page-number or footer chrome elements were found in the DOM at all in any of the 4 decks (page numbers are evidently rendered via JS/CSS counters, not static markup), so that exclusion path is untested against real footer content.

Slide boundaries are found via regex `<section class="slide` and each slide's HTML is the byte range up to the next such match (or EOF for the last slide). This is robust for this corpus (verified: no nested <section class="slide..."> found) but would break if a slide's markup ever nested another top-level slide section.
